text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Report on Enemalta, the state-owned energy corporation, says the organisation is approaching bankruptcy. It recommends a review of electricity tariffs, an increase in kerosene prices, a slowdown in capital expenditure and non-renewal of an oil agreement with Libya. Under the agreement, Libya supplies oil to Malta at favourable rates and it is then refined in Sicily at Enemalta's expense. Malta pays back Libya with products and services. The report said Enemalta would save money if it bought oil on the open market.

- Medical Association of Malta says country needs a new hospital. The government is considering whether to go ahead with the building of a $150 million hospital or enlarge and refurbish the existing one.

- Foreign Minister George Vella is in Rome for talks with his Italian counterpart Lamberto Dini on Malta's relationship with the European Union. Italy has told the new Maltese government it is against its decision to freeze the island's application to join the Union but was still ready to help Malta forge a close relationship with the bloc.
